title: Binary Tree Right Side View
description:
Given the `root` of a binary tree, imagine yourself standing on the **right side** of it. Return the values of the nodes you can see ordered from **top to bottom**.

At each depth level of the tree, the visible node is the rightmost non-null node at that depth (which may reside in the left subtree if the right subtree does not reach that depth).
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [0, 2000].
hints: You need exactly one node value per level of the binary tree: the rightmost node at that level.
In a level-order BFS, process all `levelSize` nodes of the current depth; the last node popped in each level is visible from the right side.
Alternatively, a right-first DFS (`node.right` before `node.left`) that records the first node encountered at each new depth solves it in O(n) time and O(h) space.

examples.explanation: Level 0 rightmost is 1, level 1 rightmost is 3, and level 2 rightmost is 4.
The right subtree stops at depth 1 (node 3), so nodes 4 and 5 from the deeper left subtree are visible from the right.
An empty tree has no visible nodes.
